question: Under what circumstances can an accused challenge the legality of an arrest?

## Circumstances Under Which an Accused Can Challenge the Legality of an Arrest

Based on the retrieved legal evidence, the following circumstances permit an accused to challenge the legality of an arrest:

### 1. Failure to Furnish "Reasons to Believe" or Grounds of Arrest
- Under **Section 19(1) of the PML Act**, the accused is entitled to challenge their arrest if the "reasons to believe" are not furnished to them. The Supreme Court in **Radhika Agarwal vs Union of India** held that these reasons must be supplied so the accused can challenge the validity of their arrest. Exceptions are available only in one-off cases where appropriate redactions are permissible. *(Radhika Agarwal vs Union of India, Supreme Court, 27 February 2025)*
- Under **Article 22(1) of the Constitution** and **Section 47 of BNSS 2023** (equivalent to Section 50 of CrPC 1973), grounds of arrest must be communicated in writing at the time of arrest or the earliest possible instance. Non-communication constitutes a violation of the accused's constitutional right, enabling them to challenge the arrest. *(Mihir Rajesh Shah vs The State of Maharashtra, Supreme Court, 6 November 2025)*

### 2. Through Judicial Review of the Arrest
- Courts possess an inherent power of **judicial review** over the legality of arrest, permissible both **before and after** criminal proceedings or prosecution complaints are filed. The material relied upon by the arresting authority must be **admissible before a court of law**. *(Radhika Agarwal vs Union of India, Supreme Court, 27 February 2025)*

### 3. When Arrest Is Malafide or Irregular
Under **Article 226 or Article 32** of the Constitution, judicial intervention is warranted when the arrest is:
- **Prima facie malafide**;
- Prompted by **extraneous circumstances**;
- Made in **contravention of or breach of provisions** of the concerned statute; or
- Made by an authority that **lacks the requisite authority** to arrest. *(Radhika Agarwal vs Union of India, Supreme Court, 27 February 2025)*

### 4. When Arrest Occurs While in Custody for a Different Offence
- The accused can challenge arrest even while in custody for a different offence, as procedural law does not preclude arrest for a separate offence. The accused retains the statutory right to apply for **anticipatory bail** regardless of existing custody. *(Dhanraj Aswani vs Amar S Mulchandani, Supreme Court, 9 September 2024)*

### 5. Right to Legal Aid at First Production
- The accused has the right to consult and be defended by a legal practitioner when first produced before a Magistrate. The Magistrate must inform the accused of this right, flowing from **Articles 21 and 22(1)** of the Constitution. *(Sunita Devi vs The State of Bihar, Supreme Court, 17 May 2024)*

### Important Caveat
The retrieved evidence also notes that there is **no absolute rule** that a defective arrest vitiates all connected investigative procedures. The effect of any procedural lapse must be assessed in context, considering the nature of the investigation and the circumstances of the case. *(Mihir Rajesh Shah vs The State of Maharashtra, Supreme Court, 6 November 2025)*
